MY ADVICE TO REP THOMAS MASSIE 

Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) has reignited a constitutional showdown by filing articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of bypassing Congress to launch military action in Iran. Massie, known for his strict adherence to the Constitution, argues that the administration has overstepped its authority — and he’s not backing down, even as the political pressure builds. His move isn’t just symbolic: a House vote could come as early as Wednesday, making this one of the most consequential challenges to executive power in recent months.

Hegseth fired back in a rare Pentagon press conference, calling the effort a “farce” and a political stunt — but he didn’t back down from his actions in Iran, doubling down on the administration’s military posture. President Trump has already thrown his support behind Hegseth, framing the impeachment push as an attack on his national security agenda. Still, the optics are tense: a defense secretary defending war decisions in real time, while a lone House member tries to force a constitutional check.

What’s making this even more unpredictable is that Massie isn’t acting alone — there are signs that some Democrats and even a few Republicans are open to examining Hegseth’s actions, though not necessarily through impeachment. The debate isn’t just about Iran; it’s about how much power a defense secretary can wield without congressional approval. And with tensions still high in the region, every move in D.C. is being watched overseas.

This feels like one of those moments where a single lawmaker can shift the conversation — not because he has the majority, but because he’s forcing a debate no one else wanted to have. If you’re following this, are you more focused on the constitutional angle, or how it might play out in the next election?
